thread:
Maria (PM): Quick sync — post-launch grooming for Wavefront. We got two high-severity customer bugs (one runtime leak, one ordering edge case) and a pile of small UX asks. Need to decide what lands in a 2-week follow-up vs. what gets a hotfix. TL;DR: can we commit to a 48h mitigation + 3 scoped follow-on items?

Alex (Eng): Can you drop repros + logs? I skimmed metrics — small but recurring spike.

Jamal (PD): Repro attached in the customer ticket thread, but the ordering issue shows up when users enable streaming + batching.

Sasha (SRE): Leak is in the rate limiter path. If real, it's high risk. Quick estimate: full fix ~3 dev-days + 1 QA day, touches runtime pooling.

Alex (Eng): Alternative quick mitigation: reduce default batch size and tighten token TTL for KV cache. Low-risk, reversible. Roughly 1 dev-hour + config rollout. Throughput drops ~5-10% in preliminary sim.

Maria (PM): Proposal: 1) Ship config mitigation as patch within 48h. 2) Schedule the full leak fix in next sprint (canary + rollout). 3) Pick 1 small UX enhancement to include in that 2-week follow-up (onboarding flow tweak) so customers see progress. 4) Formalize canary: 25% -> 100% over 6h with automatic rollback on error rate > 1%.

Sasha (SRE): Agree with mitigation first. For canary, add CPU and alloc-failure alerts: if CPU > 85% for 10m or OOM-like events, rollback.

Alex (Eng): I'll open a small patch branch for the config change. Patch will be: 
```yaml
# runtime config override
rate_limiter:
  max_batch: 64  # from 128
  kv_ttl_ms: 3000
```
I'll include a feature-flag so we can toggle quickly.

Jamal (PD): For the ordering enhancement customer asked for deterministic sequence when streaming — spec is nontrivial. Can we scope to a follow-on milestone rather than this hotfix?

Maria (PM): Yes, move deterministic ordering to Milestone B. For the 2-week iteration (Milestone A) we commit: mitigation patch, onboarding UX polish, and monitoring/alerting improvements.

Alex (Eng): Ack. Creating tickets now.

product-bot: Created tickets: RD-3248 (patch: rate-limiter mitigation), RD-3249 (onboarding polish), RD-3250 (monitoring thresholds). Assigned RD-3248 -> Alex (Eng).

Alex (Eng): RD-3248 created and assigned. I'll land a draft PR for the config change within 6h.

Sasha (SRE): I'll add the alert runbook and canary policy to RD-3250. Planning a brief rollback test in staging after PR merges.

Maria (PM): Quick decisions checklist: 
- Patch mitigation -> ship in 48h :white_check_mark:
- Full leak fix -> schedule in next sprint :calendar:
- Deterministic ordering -> move to Milestone B :arrow_right:
- Onboarding polish -> include in Milestone A :sparkles:
- Monitoring/alerting updates -> RD-3250 :mag:

Alex (Eng): One ask: after mitigation, let's monitor tail latency for 72h. I'll add a dashboard tile.

Jamal (PD): Also ping support for a short note to the affected customers that we have a mitigation rolling and a timeline for full fix. Keeps them calm.

Maria (PM): Good call. @support please send a 1-sentence update once patch is live.

Alex (Eng): Patch PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1204 (WIP).

Sasha (SRE): I'll pair on verification. If we see any regressions, we'll roll back the flag instantly.

Maria (PM): Thanks team. If no objections by EOD we'll go ahead with the 48h plan. :rocket:

Alex (Eng): No objections.

Jamal (PD): 👍

Sasha (SRE): 👍

Maria (PM): Closing the thread — will follow up with sprint assignment and updated milestone doc.
